shots.narration: Route Nine crosses the Hollow Mile after midnight. Every driver knows the one rule.
shots.image_prompt: A tiny old bus with glowing headlights crawling along an empty wet road through thick fog, bare twisted trees leaning over it, rain, vast empty darkness. The bus is small in the lower centre.

shots.narration: Never stop after the twelfth stop. Not for anyone.
shots.image_prompt: A lone wooden bus shelter with an empty bench under a single flickering lamp, rain and fog all around it, wet road in the foreground, nobody there. The shelter is in the centre.

shots.narration: Mara had driven this route for twenty years, and she had never once broken it.
shots.image_prompt: Mara in profile at the bus steering wheel, tired eyes fixed on the road ahead, rain-streaked windscreen glowing faintly behind her, dim dashboard light on her face.

shots.narration: Tonight, rain hammered the roof, and the bus was empty.
shots.image_prompt: Interior of the old bus looking down the long aisle from the back: rows of empty seats, rain streaming down the dark windows, dim flickering ceiling lights, tiny Mara alone at the driver's seat at the far end.

shots.narration: At the twelfth stop, an empty shelter flickered under a single lamp. Mara drove straight past.
shots.image_prompt: View through the bus side window and windscreen: the empty bus shelter under its flickering lamp sliding past on the right in fog and rain, motion streaks, Mara's gloved hands tight on the wheel in the foreground.

shots.narration: Then she glanced up at the mirror.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme close-up of the bus rear-view mirror with the dim interior of the bus reflected inside it, Mara's tired eye reflected at its edge, rain light glinting.

shots.narration: Someone was sitting in the back seat.
shots.image_prompt: The last row of the dark bus seen small and far away at the end of the aisle: a tall black silhouette sitting perfectly upright in the back seat, wide ragged hat, no face, absolute stillness, dim light.

shots.narration: She had checked the doors. They had never opened.
shots.image_prompt: Mara glancing sideways in terror, wide eyes, sweat on her temple, one hand frozen on the wheel, the bus's folding door shut tight behind her with rain on its glass.

shots.narration: He was tall and thin, in a long black coat that dripped onto the floor.
shots.image_prompt: The Tally Man seated in the aisle seat, impossibly tall and thin, a puddle of black water spreading on the floor under his dripping long coat, wide hat brim above, seen from a low angle.

shots.narration: His face was hidden beneath a ragged hat, and his fingers were far too long.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme close-up of the Tally Man's long, pale, bony fingers wrapped around the metal seat rail, far too many knuckles, the shadow of his ragged hat brim across the top of the frame.

shots.narration: Tick. Tick. Tick.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme close-up of a long yellowed fingernail carving a fresh notch into a wooden stick, wood shavings falling, deep shadow, hatching.

shots.narration: Mara's voice shook. Sir, this bus is out of service.
shots.image_prompt: Mara turning her head slightly toward the back, mouth trembling and barely open, eyes wet, in the foreground in profile; the blurred dark shape of the tall hatted figure far behind her in the mirror.

shots.narration: He did not answer. He only leaned forward, and the ticking stopped.
shots.image_prompt: The Tally Man leaning slowly forward out of his seat into the aisle, wide hat brim dripping, long fingers gripping the seatbacks on either side, the empty aisle stretching behind him, dim light.

shots.narration: She blinked. He was three rows closer.
shots.image_prompt: Point of view down the aisle from the driver's seat: the Tally Man now standing in the middle of the aisle, tall and still, head bowed under the hat, the empty seats and rain-streaked windows on both sides.

shots.narration: She blinked again. Closer.
shots.image_prompt: Mara's back and the top of her cap in the foreground, bottom of frame; looming directly over her shoulder just behind the driver's seat the huge shadow of the Tally Man's hat and face-void, long fingers reaching for her seat.

shots.narration: She slammed the accelerator to the floor.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme close-up of Mara's worn boot stomping the accelerator pedal to the floor, the speedometer needle pinned past the maximum glowing beside it, motion streaks.

shots.narration: Trees tore past. Every mile marker read thirteen, and the road never ended.
shots.image_prompt: The bus speeding down an endless straight road through fog, bare trees streaking past as black motion lines, white roadside mile marker posts each painted with the number 13 flickering by on both sides, perspective stretching to infinity.

shots.narration: Then she saw what he carried: a long wooden stick, covered in notches.
shots.image_prompt: In the rear-view mirror: the Tally Man standing behind her holding upright a long wooden stick whose entire length is covered in rows of cut notches that glint in the dim light, the black hat looming above.

shots.narration: Hundreds of notches. One for every driver who ever stopped.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme close-up of the surface of the wooden stick packed with hundreds of tiny carved notches in neat rows, some old and weathered, the last few fresh and pale, dramatic raking light.

shots.narration: And Mara remembered. Years ago, in the rain, she had stopped once, for a child at the twelfth stop.
shots.image_prompt: Flashback: a small child in a hooded raincoat standing alone under the flickering lamp in the bus shelter, an old bus with open doors glowing at the kerb, heavy rain, fog, bleak and sad.

shots.narration: But the child never wanted a ride. She wanted a driver.
shots.image_prompt: Close-up of the child's pale face under the dark raincoat hood, enormous unblinking black eyes, a thin smile that is far too wide, rain dripping off the hood, unsettling and wrong.

shots.narration: The bus rolled to a stop. The doors opened by themselves.
shots.image_prompt: The old bus stopped beside the lonely shelter in fog and rain, its folding doors swung wide open onto a glowing black interior, headlights lighting the mist, nobody in sight.

shots.narration: The Tally Man carved one final notch.
shots.image_prompt: Extreme close-up of the pale long fingers pressing a freshly carved notch into the wooden stick, wood chips flying, deep black background, one thin ray of light.

shots.narration: Now Mara waits in the shelter at the twelfth stop, soaked and smiling, watching the headlights.
shots.image_prompt: Mara standing very still under the flickering shelter lamp, soaked through, hair plastered to her face, a smile far too wide on her tired face, eyes empty and dark, two blurry headlight glows approaching in the fog behind her.

shots.narration: So if you ever drive Route Nine after midnight, and someone waits in the rain at the twelfth stop...
shots.image_prompt: Driver's point of view through a rain-streaked windscreen at night: wet road ahead, headlights cutting the fog, and at the roadside a small lone figure standing motionless under a flickering lamp by a bus shelter.

shots.narration: Keep driving.
shots.image_prompt: Pitch-black frame except for two wide pale glowing eyes and a thin impossibly wide smile of a soaked woman's face lit by a failing lamp, face centred, rain, horror.

narration: Route Nine crosses the Hollow Mile after midnight. Every driver knows the one rule. Never stop after the twelfth stop. Not for anyone. Mara had driven this route for twenty years, and she had never once broken it. Tonight, rain hammered the roof, and the bus was empty. At the twelfth stop, an empty shelter flickered under a single lamp. Mara drove straight past. Then she glanced up at the mirror. Someone was sitting in the back seat. She had checked the doors. They had never opened. He was tall and thin, in a long black coat that dripped onto the floor. His face was hidden beneath a ragged hat, and his fingers were far too long. Tick. Tick. Tick. Mara's voice shook. Sir, this bus is out of service. He did not answer. He only leaned forward, and the ticking stopped. She blinked. He was three rows closer. She blinked again. Closer. She slammed the accelerator to the floor. Trees tore past. Every mile marker read thirteen, and the road never ended. Then she saw what he carried: a long wooden stick, covered in notches. Hundreds of notches. One for every driver who ever stopped. And Mara remembered. Years ago, in the rain, she had stopped once, for a child at the twelfth stop. But the child never wanted a ride. She wanted a driver. The bus rolled to a stop. The doors opened by themselves. The Tally Man carved one final notch. Now Mara waits in the shelter at the twelfth stop, soaked and smiling, watching the headlights. So if you ever drive Route Nine after midnight, and someone waits in the rain at the twelfth stop... Keep driving.
